note: What an image does decides which controls must be inspected for it. Every image inspects the controls the baseline leaves to it, or gives it; each capability an image declares adds more. The map says which, and why. A capability may also raise a control the High baseline does not select, under consider: not required, but put in front of whoever inspects, to select or to decline with a reason. It does not decide the answer: inspecting a control is a person's work, recorded in the image's cyber package. See docs/CYBER-PACKAGE.md.

authenticates-clients.title: Authenticates clients
authenticates-clients.question: Does the image verify a credential itself: a token, a session, a password, a certificate?
authenticates-clients.why: It authenticates, even where an identity provider issued the credential, so identification and session controls apply to it.

authorizes-by-claims.title: Authorizes from claims or roles
authorizes-by-claims.question: Does the image decide what a caller may do, from claims, roles, or policy it holds?
authorizes-by-claims.why: The image enforces access, and least privilege applies to what it permits.

issues-credentials.title: Issues credentials
issues-credentials.question: Does the image issue tokens, API keys, or access keys that a client uses later?
issues-credentials.why: An issued credential is an authenticator the image manages, and its use must be attributable.

consider.label: IA-5(13)
consider.title: Expiration of Cached Authenticators
consider.why: An image that issues tokens decides how long they remain usable; the High baseline does not select this, and a token with no expiry is worth a deliberate decision.

manages-accounts.title: Manages accounts
manages-accounts.question: Does the image create, store, disable, or attribute accounts of its own?
manages-accounts.why: Account management is then the image's, not only the organization's.

offers-admin-interface.title: Offers an administrative interface
offers-admin-interface.question: Does the image expose an interface that configures or administers it?
offers-admin-interface.why: An administrative path is privileged access, and is where most SRG rules about management interfaces land.

processes-untrusted-content.title: Processes content it did not produce
processes-untrusted-content.question: Does the image parse, render, or execute content supplied by a caller or a tenant?
processes-untrusted-content.why: Input validation and mobile code apply where the image acts on something a caller sent.

consider.label: SI-15
consider.title: Information Output Filtering
consider.why: An image that renders or transforms content a caller supplied can emit what that caller put in; output filtering is not in the High baseline, and is worth selecting where it can.

runs-several-roles.title: Runs as more than one role
runs-several-roles.question: Does one image run as different roles, such as a server and its workers?
runs-several-roles.why: Each role has its own surface, and the traffic between them is inside the system, not outside it.

consider.label: IA-9
consider.title: Service Identification and Authentication
consider.why: Roles of one image authenticate to each other; the baseline does not select a control for that, and the platform's PLT-18 covers only what the platform can impose.

sends-email.title: Sends or receives mail
sends-email.question: Does the image handle electronic mail in any form?
sends-email.why: Mail brings its own controls, which are otherwise inapplicable.

serves-http.title: Serves or proxies HTTP
serves-http.question: Does the image answer HTTP requests, for content, an API, or as a proxy?
serves-http.why: What it serves, to whom, and what it logs and rejects becomes the image's business.

stores-data.title: Stores data that outlives the container
stores-data.question: Does the image write data meant to persist, to a volume or an object store?
stores-data.why: Data at rest, its protection, and its disposal become the image's concern as well as the platform's.

talks-to-other-services.title: Calls other services
talks-to-other-services.question: Does the image open outbound connections to services of its own, such as a database or a peer?
talks-to-other-services.why: What it connects to, and how that traffic is authenticated and protected, is part of the image's design.

consider.label: IA-9
consider.title: Service Identification and Authentication
consider.why: Where an image calls services of its own, how those services prove who they are is not covered by the baseline's user-facing identification controls.

terminates-mutual-tls.title: Terminates mutual TLS
terminates-mutual-tls.question: Does the image verify a client certificate, and decide anything from it?
terminates-mutual-tls.why: Verifying a client certificate is authentication, and what follows from it is access enforcement.

terminates-tls.title: Terminates TLS
terminates-tls.question: Does the image itself terminate TLS, with key material it is given?
terminates-tls.why: It then holds key material and chooses the protocol and ciphers, whoever issued the certificate.
